Claims regarding the efficacy, safety, and liability of Covid-19 vaccines continue to circulate widely on social media. A recent post asserts that, for the Covid-19 vaccines currently approved in Germany, there are no clinical studies proving their efficacy and safety, and furthermore, that no one is liable for vaccine damage. This article examines these claims in detail, providing context and verifiable information.

To begin, several Covid-19 vaccines are approved for use in Germany, including those developed by BioNTech/Pfizer, Moderna, AstraZeneca, and Johnson & Johnson. Each of these vaccines underwent rigorous clinical trials before receiving approval from the European Medicines Agency (EMA) and the Paul-Ehrlich-Institut, Germany’s federal institute for vaccines. These trials are designed to test both efficacy (how well the vaccine works to prevent disease) and safety (whether the vaccine causes adverse effects).

Clinical trials for Covid-19 vaccines typically followed a phased approach. In Phase I, researchers assessed safety in a small group of volunteers. Phase II expanded the trial to hundreds of participants to further evaluate safety and immune response. Phase III involved thousands to tens of thousands of participants, with the aim of determining how well the vaccines protect against Covid-19 and monitoring for side effects. The data from Phase III trials for the vaccines approved in Germany showed high efficacy rates in preventing symptomatic Covid-19 and a favorable safety profile, with most side effects being mild or moderate. These results were scrutinized by regulatory authorities before approval was granted.

Since approval, ongoing monitoring—known as pharmacovigilance—has been in place to track any rare or long-term side effects. The Paul-Ehrlich-Institut regularly publishes safety updates, and reported adverse events are reviewed and investigated. This post-market surveillance is standard for all vaccines and medicines.

The claim that “no one is liable for vaccine damage” requires clarification. In Germany, vaccine injuries are covered under the Infection Protection Act (Infektionsschutzgesetz). Individuals who suffer damage to health as a result of a publicly recommended vaccination, including those for Covid-19, may be entitled to compensation from the state. This protection is not dependent on whether the manufacturer is liable; rather, it is a public responsibility. Furthermore, vaccine manufacturers may be held liable if defects in the vaccine or breach of regulatory standards are proven. However, the government assumes primary responsibility for compensation related to recommended vaccines.

In summary, contrary to the social media claim, all Covid-19 vaccines approved in Germany underwent extensive clinical trials demonstrating efficacy and safety before authorization. Post-market surveillance continues to ensure ongoing safety monitoring. Additionally, those who experience vaccine-related injury are not without recourse; compensation mechanisms exist under German law. It remains crucial to rely on verified information from public health authorities and scientific sources when evaluating claims about vaccines.

Změny ohledně účinnosti, bezpečnosti a odpovědnosti vakcín proti covidu-19 se šíří široce na sociálních sítích. Nedávný příspěvek tvrdí, že pro vakcíny proti covidu-19 schválené v Německu neexistují klinické studie, které by prokázaly jejich účinnost a bezpečnost, a dále, že nikdo nenese odpovědnost za poškození způsobené vakcínou. Tento článek detailně zkoumá tyto tvrzení, poskytuje kontext a ověřitelné informace.

Začneme tím, že v Německu jsou schváleny několik vakcín proti covidu-19, včetně těch vyvinutých společností BioNTech/Pfizer, Moderna, AstraZeneca a Johnson & Johnson. Každá z těchto vakcín prošla rigorózními klinickými studiemi před schválením ze strany Evropské agentské ústavy pro léčivá (EMA) a Německého státního ústavu pro vakcíny (Paul-Ehrlich-Institut). Tyto studie jsou navrženy tak, aby testovaly jak účinnost (jak dobře vakcína zabrání nemoci), tak bezpečnost (zda vakcína způsobuje nepříznivé účinky).

Klinické studie vakcín proti covidu-19 obvykle postupovaly v fázích. V fázi I vědci hodnotili bezpečnost u malého počtu dobrovolníků. Fáze II rozšířila studii na stovky účastníků, aby dále hodnotila bezpečnost a imunitní odpověď. Fáze III zahrnovala tisíce až desetitisíce účastníků, s cílem určit, jak dobře vakcíny chrání před covidem-19 a sledovat případné vedlejší účinky. Data z fáze III studií pro vakcíny schválené v Německu ukázala vysoké úspěšnosti v předcházení příznaků covidu-19 a příznivý bezpečnostní profil, přičemž většina vedlejších účinků byla mírná nebo středně těžká. Tyto výsledky byly před schválením zkontrolovány regulačními orgány.

Od schválení vakcín byla v praxi zavedena pravidelná sledování, známá jako farmakovodba, která sleduje možné vzácné nebo dlouhodobé vedlejší účinky. Německý státní ústav pro vakcíny pravidelně zveřejňuje bezpečnostní aktualizace a zpracovává a vyšetřuje hlášené nežádoucí události. Tato sledování v praxi je standardní pro všechny vakcíny i léky.

Tvrzení, že „nikdo nenese odpovědnost za poškození způsobené vakcínou“, vyžaduje vysvětlení. V Německu poškození způsobené vakcínou jsou pokryta Zákonem o ochraně proti infekcím (Infektionsschutzgesetz). Osoby, které trpí zdravotním poškozením v důsledku doporučené vakciny, včetně vakcín proti covidu-19, mohou být oprávněny k odškodnění z veřejného rozpočtu. Tato ochrana nezávisí na tom, zda je výrobce odpovědný, ale je veřejnou zodpovědností. Navíc mohou být výrobci vakcín zodpovědní, pokud jsou potvrzeny nedostatky v vakcíně nebo porušení regulačních standardů. Nicméně vláda přebírá primární zodpovědnost za odškodnění související s doporučenými vakcínami.

Shrnutí: proti tvrzení na sociálních sítích, všechny vakcíny proti covidu-19 schválené v Německu prošly rozsáhlými klinickými studiemi, které prokázaly jejich účinnost a bezpečnost před schválením. Po schválení probíhá pravidelné sledování, aby zajišťovalo průběžné monitorování bezpečnosti. Kromě toho ti, kteří zaznamenají poškození spojené s vakcínou, nemají žádné právní opory; odškodnění existuje v rámci německého zákona. Je stále důležité záviset na ověřených informacích z veřejných zdravotních orgánů a vědeckých zdrojů při hodnocení tvrzení ohledně vakcín.

A social media post has been circulating, claiming that Markus Söder, the Minister-President of Bavaria, stated: “Parents who send their children to school without vaccination should lose their legal guardianship.” This assertion has sparked heated debate online, with many users expressing outrage over what they interpret as an extreme stance on childhood vaccination policy. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is essential to examine the context in which Markus Söder has discussed vaccination, his public statements, and relevant German legislation.

Markus Söder, a prominent figure in German politics and a member of the Christian Social Union (CSU), has been a vocal advocate for vaccination, particularly in the context of public health and school attendance. In recent years, Germany has grappled with outbreaks of vaccine-preventable diseases such as measles, prompting federal and state officials to call for stricter vaccination requirements. In 2020, the German government introduced the Measles Protection Act, which mandates that children must be vaccinated against measles before attending school or daycare, except in cases of medical exemption.

Söder has consistently supported strong measures to increase vaccination rates. He has publicly emphasized the importance of protecting both individual children and the broader community from contagious diseases. In media interviews and public speeches, Söder has suggested that vaccination is a social responsibility and has called for rigorous enforcement of vaccination laws. However, a careful review of his public statements reveals no record of Söder explicitly stating that parents who send their unvaccinated children to school should lose their legal guardianship.

In fact, Söder’s remarks have generally focused on consequences such as fines or exclusion from daycare and schooling for unvaccinated children, in line with existing German law. The Measles Protection Act allows for fines of up to 2,500 euros for non-compliance, but it does not stipulate the loss of parental rights as a penalty. While Söder has occasionally used strong language to underscore the seriousness of the issue, there is no direct evidence that he has proposed stripping parents of legal guardianship solely for sending unvaccinated children to school.

It is also important to note that the loss of legal guardianship in Germany is a severe measure, typically reserved for cases involving child abuse, severe neglect, or endangerment. The legal threshold for removing a child from parental care is high and involves judicial review. Failure to vaccinate a child, while a matter of public health concern, does not automatically result in the loss of guardianship under German law.

In conclusion, the social media post misrepresents Markus Söder’s position. While Söder is a strong proponent of vaccination and supports legal measures to enforce vaccination requirements, there is no verifiable statement from him advocating for the removal of parental rights in cases of non-compliance. The claim that he said “Parents who send their children to school without vaccination should lose their legal guardianship” is not supported by available evidence and appears to be a distortion of his actual views and the legal framework in Germany.

సోషల్ మీడియాలో విస్తృతంగా వ్యాపించిన ఒక పోస్ట్ ప్రకారం, బావియా మంత్రి మార్క్స్ సోడర్ అనే వ్యక్తి ఇలా అన్నారు: "వ్యాక్సినేషన్ లేకుండా పిల్లలను పాఠశాలకు పంపే తల్లిదండ్రులకు కాయిదె ప్రాధాన్యత కోల్పోవాలి." ఈ వాదన ఆన్లైన్లో వివాదాలకు కారణమైంది, అంతేకాకుండా కొంతమంది వాడుకరులు పిల్లల వ్యాక్సినేషన్ నిబంధనలపై అంతర్జాలంలో చెప్పిన వాదన అతిగా ఉండటం వల్ల ఆగ్రహం వ్యక్తం చేశారు. ఈ వాదన సరియైనదో కాదో అంచనా వేయడానికి, మార్క్స్ సోడర్ వ్యాక్సినేషన్ విషయంలో చర్చించిన స్థితి, ప్రభుత్వ ప్రకటనలు మరియు సంబంధిత జర్మన్ చట్టాల గురించి పరిశీలించాలి.

జర్మన్ రాజకీయంలో ప్రముఖుడు మరియు క్రైస్టియన్ సోషల్ యూనియన్ (CSU) సభ్యుడైన మార్క్స్ సోడర్, ప్రజా ఆరోగ్యం మరియు పాఠశాల సందర్శన విషయంలో వ్యాక్సినేషన్ నిబంధనలకు అండగా ఉండాలని స్పష్టంగా వాదిస్తూ వస్తున్నాడు. గత కొంతకాలంగా, మెస్సెల్ వ్యాక్సినేషన్ నిబంధనలు అనుసరించడం లేకుండా వ్యాక్సినేషన్ చేయని వ్యాధులు మరియు మెస్సెల్ వంటి వ్యాక్సినేషన్ చేయని వ్యాధుల మార్పులు జరిగాయి, అందువల్ల సంఘపు మరియు రాష్ట్ర అధికారులు వ్యాక్సినేషన్ ప్రాధాన్యత పెంచడానికి కట్టుబాటు విధానాలకు పిలుపు ఇచ్చారు. 2020లో, జర్మన్ ప్రభుత్వం మెస్సెల్ రక్షణ చట్టాన్ని ప్రవేశపెట్టింది, దీని ప్రకారం పాఠశాల లేదా చిన్నారుల కేర్ కు వెళ్ళడానికి ముందు పిల్లలకు మెస్సెల్ వ్యాక్సినేషన్ చేయాలి, అయితే ఆరోగ్య విధి తప్పుడు సందర్భంలో అనుమతి ఉండవచ్చు.

సోడర్ వ్యాక్సినేషన్ నిబంధనల ప్రాధాన్యతను పెంచడానికి ప్రముఖ చర్యలు సమర్థించాడు. అతను ప్రజా ఆరోగ్యం మరియు సామాజిక సౌలభ్యం విషయంలో విషయాలను ప్రాధాన్యత ఇస్తున్నాడు. మీడియా ఇంటర్వ్యూలు మరియు ప్రజా ప్రసంగాలలో సోడర్ వ్యాక్సినేషన్ ఒక సామాజిక బాధ్యత అని పేర్కొని, వ్యాక్సినేషన్ చట్టాల అమలు కోసం విధి విధానాలు వాడాలని అనుకూలంగా ఉంచాడు. అయితే అతని ప్రామాణిక ప్రకటనల పరిశీలన ద్వారా సోడర్ వ్యాక్సినేషన్ లేని పిల్లలను పాఠశాలకు పంపే తల్లిదండ్రులకు కాయిదె ప్రాధాన్యత కోల్పోవాలని స్పష్టంగా అన్నాడు అని నమ్మిన విషయం లేదు.

అంతేకాకుండా సోడర్ వ్యాక్సినేషన్ విషయంలో వాదన కూడా వివాదాల విషయంలో ప్రముఖ విధానం విషయంలో ప్రాముఖ్యత ఇచ్చినట్లు తెలుస్తుంది, వ్యాక్సినేషన్ లేని పిల్లల కోసం జర్మన్ చట్టాలకు అనుగుణంగా ప్రామాణిక బాధ్యతలు ప్రాధాన్యత ఇచ్చాడు. మెస్సెల్ రక్షణ చట్టం అనుసరించని వారికి వ్యవస్థాపక విధానం విషయంలో రూ. 2,500 వరకు శిక్ష ఇస్తుంది, కానీ కాయిదె ప్రాధాన్యత కోల్పోవడం వంటి శిక్ష ఇచ్చే విధంగా కాదు. సోడర్ సమస్య యొక్క గంభీరతను పేర్కొనడానికి వివిధ వాక్యాలు ఉపయోగించాడు, కానీ అతను వ్యాక్సినేషన్ లేని పిల్లలను పాఠశాలకు పంపే తల్లిదండ్రులకు కాయిదె ప్రాధాన్యత కోల్పోవడం వంటి ప్రతిపాదనను సంపూర్ణంగా అందించాడు అని స్పష్టంగా ప్రమాణం లేదు.

గుర్తించాలి కూడా, జర్మన్ చట్టంలో కాయిదె ప్రాధాన్యత కోల్పోవడం అత్యంత విధి విధానం, ఇది చిన్నారి అత్యాచారం, విపత్తు లేదా చిన్నారి ప్రాణాలకు ప్రాణాల ప్రాధాన్యత కోల్పోవడం వంటి సందర్భాలలో మాత్రమే ఉంటుంది. పిల్లల ప్రాణాలను కాపాడేందుకు ప్రామాణిక చట్టం చట్టాలకు అనుగుణంగా విధి విధానం అనుమతి ఇస్తుంది. పిల్లల వ్యాక్సినేషన్ లేకుండా ఉండటం ప్రజా ఆరోగ్య విషయం అయినప్పటికీ, జర్మన్ చట్టంలో కాయిదె ప్రాధాన్యత కోల్పోవడం స్వయంగా కాదు.

ప్రస్తావించిన సోషల్ మీడియా పోస్ట్ మార్క్స్ సోడర్ విషయంలో అసత్యాలను ప్రదర్శిస్తుంది. సోడర్ వ్యాక్సినేషన్ కు ప్రముఖ మద్దతు ఇస్తున్నాడు మరియు వ్యాక్సినేషన్ నిబంధనలను అమలు చేసే చట్టాలకు సంబంధించి విధి విధానాలను సమర్థిస్తున్నాడు, కానీ వాటి ప్రామాణిక ప్రకటనల అంచనా వేయడం లేదు. సోడర్ వివాదం అంటే "వ్యాక్సినేషన్ లేకుండా పాఠశాలకు పంపే తల్లిదండ్రులకు కాయిదె ప్రాధాన్యత కోల్పోవాలి" అని చెప్పిన వాదన సమర్థించడానికి సమాధానం లేదు మరియు దీని సాధ్యత లేదు.

In August 2021, social media users circulated claims suggesting that, despite widespread COVID-19 vaccination efforts, the number of coronavirus cases was four times higher than in August 2020. This assertion raises questions about the effectiveness of vaccines and the factors influencing pandemic trends. To provide a thorough understanding, it is essential to examine the context, background, and the accuracy of this claim.

First, let us consider the timeline and the state of the pandemic in August 2020 versus August 2021. In August 2020, COVID-19 was still a relatively new global threat. While many countries had experienced their first waves, strict public health measures, such as lockdowns, mask mandates, and travel restrictions, were widely enforced. Vaccines were not yet available to the general public; clinical trials were ongoing, and vaccination campaigns would not begin until late 2020 and early 2021.

By contrast, August 2021 marked a period when vaccination programs had accelerated worldwide. In many countries, a significant proportion of adults had received at least one dose of COVID-19 vaccine, with millions fully vaccinated. Governments and health authorities had relaxed some restrictions, relying on vaccine-induced immunity to curb the spread and severity of the virus.

When comparing case numbers between these two periods, it is true that global daily reported cases in August 2021 were higher than in August 2020. For example, in numerous countries, including the United States and the United Kingdom, the Delta variant had become the dominant strain. Delta is known for its higher transmissibility compared to earlier versions of the coronavirus. This contributed to a surge in reported cases, even in populations with substantial vaccine coverage.

However, the comparison of raw case numbers between the two periods without context can be misleading. Several factors influenced the rise in cases in August 2021:

1. **Variant Impact**: The Delta variant spread rapidly and was more contagious than previous variants circulating in 2020. This led to increased transmission rates and higher case counts.

2. **Testing Capacity**: Testing infrastructure expanded significantly between 2020 and 2021. In August 2020, many regions faced limited testing availability, resulting in underreported case numbers. By August 2021, more extensive and accessible testing meant more cases were detected and reported.

3. **Behavioral Changes**: As vaccines rolled out, restrictions eased, and people resumed social activities. Increased mobility and gatherings contributed to greater opportunities for the virus to spread.

4. **Vaccine Effectiveness**: Vaccines primarily reduce severe illness, hospitalization, and death. While breakthrough infections can occur, especially with highly transmissible variants, evidence shows that vaccinated individuals are much less likely to experience severe outcomes than those who are unvaccinated.

In summary, while the number of reported COVID-19 cases in August 2021 was indeed higher—sometimes up to four times greater—than in August 2020, attributing this solely to vaccine ineffectiveness is incorrect. The higher case counts resulted from the emergence of the Delta variant, increased testing, and changes in public behavior, not a failure of vaccines. Crucially, even as cases increased, hospitalizations and deaths did not rise at the same rate, underscoring the protective effect of vaccination against severe disease. The claim, while accurate in its numbers, lacks critical context and does not fully represent the complex reality of pandemic trends.

W sierpniu 2021 roku użytkownicy mediów społecznościowych powszechnie obiegali tezy sugerujące, że mimo szerokiej kampanii szczepień przeciwko wirusowi SARS-CoV-2 liczba zarejestrowanych przypadków koronawirusa była cztery razy wyższa niż w sierpniu 2020 roku. Taka teza budzi pytania dotyczące skuteczności szczepionek oraz czynników wpływających na tendencje pandemii. Aby zapewnić kompletny obraz, konieczne jest przeanalizowanie kontekstu, tła oraz poprawności tej tezy.

Początek, rozważmy czasownik i sytuację pandemii w sierpniu 2020 roku w porównaniu do sierpnia 2021 roku. W sierpniu 2020 roku koronawirus był nadal nowym globalnym zagrożeniem. Choć wiele krajów doświadczyło pierwszych fal zachorowań, obowiązywały ścisłe środki profilaktyczne, takie jak lockdowny, obowiązki noszenia masztek oraz ograniczenia podróży. Szczepionki były jeszcze niedostępne dla ogółu ludności; badania kliniczne trwały, a kampanie szczepienne zostały zainicjowane dopiero w późnych miesiącach 2020 roku i wczesnych miesiącach 2021 roku.

W przeciwieństwie do tego, sierpień 2021 roku oznaczał okres, w którym programy szczepienia przyspieszyły na całym świecie. W wielu krajach znaczną część dorosłych otrzymało przynajmniej jedną dawkę szczepionki przeciwko koronawirusowi, a miliony osób zakończyły pełną serię szczepień. Rządy i instytucje zdrowia zwolniły część ograniczeń, opierając się na odporności wywołanej szczepionkami, by ograniczyć rozprzestrzenianie się wirusa i jego skutki.

Porównując liczby zakażeń w tych dwóch okresach, rzeczywiście liczba dziennych zarejestrowanych przypadków koronawirusa w sierpniu 2021 roku była wyższa niż w sierpniu 2020 roku. Na przykład, w wielu krajach, w tym w Stanach Zjednoczonych i Wielkiej Brytanii, dominującym szczepem był wariant Delta. Wariant Delta znany jest z większej zakaźności w porównaniu z wcześniejszymi wersjami wirusa. To przyczyniło się do wzrostu liczby zarejestrowanych przypadków, nawet w społecznościach z dużą proporcją szczepionek.

Jednak porównanie surowych liczb zakażeń między tymi okresami bez kontekstu może być mylące. Kilka czynników wpłynęło na wzrost liczby przypadków w sierpniu 2021 roku:

1. **Wpływ wariantu**: Wariant Delta rozprzestrzeniał się szybciej i był bardziej zakaźny niż wcześniejsze warianty obecne w 2020 roku. To prowadziło do zwiększenia się szybkości rozprzestrzeniania się i liczby zakażeń.

2. **Poziom testowania**: Infrastruktura testowania znacznie się rozwinęła między 2020 a 2021 rokiem. W sierpniu 2020 roku wiele regionów doświadczyło ograniczonego dostępności testów, co prowadziło do niedostatecznego zarejestrowania przypadków. W sierpniu 2021 roku dostępność testów była większa i łatwiejsza, co oznaczało wykrycie i zgłoszenie większej liczby przypadków.

3. **Zmiany zachowań**: W miarę rozwoju szczepień ograniczenia się zmniejszały, a ludzie wracali do aktywności społecznych. Zwiększone mobilność i spotkania przyczyniły się do większej możliwości rozprzestrzeniania się wirusa.

4. **Skuteczność szczepionek**: Szczepionki głównie zmniejszają poważne objawy, hospitalizację i śmiertelność. Choć mogą wystąpić przypadki zakażeń u szczepionkowanych, zwłaszcza w przypadku bardzo zakaźnych wariantów, dowody pokazują, że osoby szczepione są znacznie mniej podatne na poważne konsekwencje niż niezszepionkowani.

Podsumowując, choć liczba zarejestrowanych przypadków koronawirusa w sierpniu 2021 roku rzeczywiście była wyższa – często nawet cztery razy większa – niż w sierpniu 2020 roku, przypisywanie tego jedynie nieskuteczności szczepionek jest niepoprawne. Wzrost liczby przypadków wynikał z pojawienia się wariantu Delta, zwiększenia się testowania oraz zmian zachowań społecznych, a nie z niepowodzenia szczepionek. Ważne jest, że nawet w czasie wzrostu liczby przypadków, liczba hospitalizacji i śmiertelności nie wzrosła w takim samym tempie, co podkreśla ochronę szczepionek przed poważnymi objawami choroby. Teza, choć poprawna w liczbie przypadków, brakuje kluczowego kontekstu i nie przedstawia kompleksowego obrazu trendów pandemii.

Obwohl die Fallzahlen höher waren, blieben Hospitalisierungen und Todesfälle deutlich niedriger, was die Schutzwirkung der Impfungen unterstreicht.

The claim that “Ivermectin is an effective drug against Covid-19” has circulated widely on social media, especially since the early stages of the pandemic. To assess its accuracy, it is important to examine the background of the drug, the scientific evidence available, and the conclusions reached by health authorities and experts.

Ivermectin is an antiparasitic medication that has been used for decades to treat various conditions such as river blindness and scabies. Its safety profile for those uses is well-established, and it has contributed significantly to global health. In 2020 and 2021, as the Covid-19 pandemic intensified, some researchers and individuals began to speculate about the potential antiviral effects of Ivermectin, partly based on laboratory studies that showed the drug could inhibit the replication of certain viruses in cell cultures.

These preliminary laboratory findings sparked interest and led to several clinical trials around the world. Some small studies suggested that Ivermectin could have a beneficial effect in reducing symptoms or shortening the duration of Covid-19. However, many of these early studies were limited by methodological flaws, small sample sizes, or inconsistencies in dosing and protocols. Subsequent larger and more rigorous studies, including randomized controlled trials, did not find convincing evidence that Ivermectin was effective in treating or preventing Covid-19.

Major health organizations, including the World Health Organization and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, have reviewed the available data on Ivermectin’s use in Covid-19. Their findings indicate that the evidence does not support the use of Ivermectin for this purpose. They have advised against using the drug outside of well-conducted clinical trials, citing the lack of reliable data showing significant benefit and the potential risks associated with improper use. In some cases, individuals have self-medicated with veterinary formulations of Ivermectin, leading to serious health consequences.

The scientific consensus is that the most effective ways to prevent and treat Covid-19 are vaccination, antiviral medications specifically authorized for Covid-19, and supportive medical care. While research continues into new treatments and potential uses for existing drugs, claims about Ivermectin as an effective Covid-19 therapy are not substantiated by current high-quality evidence.

It is important for the public to rely on credible sources and up-to-date research when considering treatments for Covid-19. The spread of misinformation can undermine public health efforts and potentially put individuals at risk. At present, the claim that Ivermectin is an effective drug against Covid-19 is not supported by robust scientific data and is contradicted by the guidance of global health authorities. Individuals seeking protection or treatment for Covid-19 should consult healthcare professionals and follow recommendations based on the latest scientific evidence.

A social media post has been circulating, claiming that Bertram Häussler stated “Corona was not the cause of death in 80 percent of official Covid deaths.” This assertion has generated significant public discussion and confusion regarding the accuracy of official Covid-19 death counts in Germany and beyond. To assess the veracity of this claim, it is important to examine the context of Häussler’s statements, the methodology behind Covid-19 death reporting, and the nuances of cause-of-death attribution during the pandemic.

**Background and Context**

Bertram Häussler is a respected German health researcher and the head of the IGES Institute, a health research organization. Throughout the Covid-19 pandemic, Häussler has frequently commented on the interpretation of Covid-19 data in Germany, including hospitalization and mortality statistics.

The claim in question references statements made by Häussler during interviews and public discussions, particularly in relation to the official counting methods used for Covid-19 deaths. According to standard German reporting procedures, anyone who dies after testing positive for SARS-CoV-2 is counted as a Covid-19 death, regardless of the immediate cause of death. This method is intended to ensure comprehensive reporting and comparability across regions, but it has also sparked debate over whether all reported Covid-19 deaths are truly caused by the virus.

**Analysis of the Claim**

The social media post asserts that Häussler said “Corona was not the cause of death in 80 percent of official Covid deaths.” This statement is a paraphrase and simplification of points Häussler has made, particularly regarding the distinction between dying “with” and “from” Covid-19. In several interviews, Häussler has suggested that, especially during later phases of the pandemic, a significant proportion of individuals recorded as Covid-19 deaths were people who died with a Covid-19 infection, but whose primary cause of death was another serious illness, such as heart disease, cancer, or advanced age-related conditions.

However, the specific figure of 80 percent is not a universally accepted or consistently reported statistic. Häussler has at times referenced high percentages—up to 80 percent in certain weeks or contexts—of deaths among people who were infected with Covid-19 but had other underlying fatal conditions. Nevertheless, this does not mean that Covid-19 played no role in these deaths; for many, the infection could have worsened pre-existing conditions or contributed to a fatal outcome.

It is crucial to note that official death certificates in Germany, as in many other countries, distinguish between the “immediate” cause of death and contributing factors. Covid-19 may be listed as a contributing factor rather than the immediate cause, but it is still considered significant in the fatal outcome.

**Conclusion**

The claim that Bertram Häussler said “Corona was not the cause of death in 80 percent of official Covid deaths” is a partial and context-dependent representation of his statements. While Häussler has pointed out that many people who died with Covid-19 infections had other serious health conditions, and that the direct causality of the virus in each death varies, the statement oversimplifies a complex issue. It is not accurate to conclude that Covid-19 was irrelevant in 80 percent of deaths; rather, the data suggest a nuanced relationship between infection and mortality, especially among the elderly and those with pre-existing conditions. As with all pandemic data, careful interpretation and context are essential to understanding the true impact of Covid-19 on mortality statistics.

Postimi në sotial media thotë se Häussler ka thënë "Korona nuk është shkaku i vdekjes në 80% të vdekjeve oficiale të koronavirusit." **Konkluzion**

Ndërsa Häussler ka përmendur se shumë persona që janë vdekur me infeksion të koronavirusit kanë kushte të tjera të shkaktueshme të vdekjes, dhe se shkaku i drejtë i virusit në secilën vdekje ndryshon, afirata e thjeshtëson një problem të kompleksë. A recent social media post claims that Christian Drosten, a prominent German virologist, stated that "the best way to be protected from contracting the coronavirus is to get infected." This assertion raises serious concerns about its accuracy, as it contradicts the general guidance issued by public health authorities and the scientific consensus on COVID-19 prevention. To assess the validity of this claim, it is important to examine Drosten’s public statements, the broader context of COVID-19 prevention, and the scientific understanding of immunity to the coronavirus.

Christian Drosten is the director of the Institute of Virology at Charité Hospital in Berlin and has played a significant role in advising the German government and the public throughout the pandemic. He is widely recognized for his expertise in coronavirus research and has been a leading voice advocating for evidence-based public health measures, including vaccination, mask-wearing, and social distancing.

The claim that Drosten recommended infection with SARS-CoV-2 as the best means of protection misrepresents both his position and established medical guidance. Throughout the pandemic, Drosten has repeatedly emphasized the importance of vaccination as the safest and most effective way to build immunity against COVID-19. While it is true that infection with the coronavirus can result in the development of some natural immunity, this approach carries significant risks, including severe illness, hospitalization, long-term health consequences, and death. Drosten has warned against underestimating these risks, especially for vulnerable populations.

Scientific studies have shown that immunity acquired through vaccination is robust and, in many cases, provides broader and longer-lasting protection than immunity from infection alone. Furthermore, vaccines reduce the risk of severe disease and complications from COVID-19. Drosten has advocated for widespread vaccination campaigns and booster doses to maintain high levels of immunity within the population and to prevent the spread of the virus.

It is possible that the social media post stems from a misunderstanding or selective interpretation of Drosten’s statements regarding hybrid immunity. Hybrid immunity refers to the enhanced immune protection observed in individuals who have both been vaccinated and experienced a prior infection. Some studies have suggested that this combination can lead to stronger and more durable immunity. However, Drosten and other experts have not recommended intentional infection as a strategy; rather, they stress that vaccination is the primary and safest path to protection, and any additional immunity from infection should be considered incidental, not deliberate.

In conclusion, the claim that Christian Drosten said the best way to be protected from contracting the coronavirus is to get infected is misleading and inaccurate. Drosten has consistently promoted vaccination and other preventive measures as the optimal approach to COVID-19 protection. Deliberately seeking infection is not recommended by Drosten or by health authorities, as it exposes individuals to unnecessary health risks. The safest and most effective way to protect oneself from COVID-19 remains vaccination and adherence to public health guidelines.

article_content:
A recent social media post has drawn attention to claims of adverse events following COVID-19 vaccinations in a senior citizens' home in Oberhausen, Germany. The post alleges that, according to a letter from a doctor, there had been one death and two resuscitations in connection with the administration of the third dose ("booster") of the COVID-19 vaccine at this facility. This report has sparked concerns about the safety of booster vaccinations, particularly among elderly populations.

To assess the accuracy of these claims, it is important to first understand the context of COVID-19 booster vaccinations in Germany. Booster shots were rolled out to increase protection, especially for vulnerable groups such as the elderly and those in care homes, as immunity from initial doses may wane over time. Like all vaccines and medical interventions, COVID-19 vaccines can have side effects, but serious adverse events are considered rare based on data from health authorities.

The social media claim centers on a letter allegedly written by a doctor, detailing that one resident died and two others required resuscitation after receiving their third COVID-19 vaccine dose. The post does not specify the date of the events, the identities of those involved, or the precise nature of the medical incidents. Crucially, the post attributes the incidents to the booster vaccination but does not provide medical evidence establishing a direct causal relationship.

Fact-checking such claims requires a careful review of official statements, medical records (where available), and context from health authorities. In past instances, similar reports about deaths or serious events occurring after vaccination have been investigated by local health departments and, in Germany, by the Paul Ehrlich Institute, which monitors vaccine safety. In the majority of cases, investigations have found that adverse events coinciding with vaccination in elderly care homes were often related to underlying health conditions or the general frailty of residents, rather than the vaccine itself.

It is not uncommon for deaths or medical emergencies to occur in senior care homes, given the advanced age and complex health profiles of residents. Therefore, temporal association with vaccination does not automatically imply causation. Health authorities emphasize the importance of comprehensive medical evaluation to determine if a vaccine played a role in such events. Without the release of a formal investigation or autopsy results, it is not possible to confirm that the booster dose was responsible for the death or the resuscitations referenced in the post.

Furthermore, public health data continue to show that the benefits of COVID-19 vaccination, including booster doses, outweigh the risks for elderly populations, who are at greater risk of severe illness from the virus itself.

In summary, while the claim references a letter from a doctor about adverse events following a booster vaccination in an Oberhausen care home, there is currently no publicly available evidence confirming that the third dose directly caused a death and two resuscitations. Such reports should be interpreted with caution until verified by health authorities through thorough investigation. The safety profile of COVID-19 vaccines remains favorable, particularly for high-risk groups.

最近，一则社交媒体帖子引发了人们对德国奥伯豪森一家养老院内接种新冠疫苗后出现不良事件的讨论。该帖子声称，根据一封医生的信件，该养老院在接种第三剂新冠疫苗（即加强针）期间，曾发生一起死亡事件和两次心肺复苏。这一报告引发了公众对加强针安全性的担忧，尤其是在老年人群体中。

为评估这些说法的真实性，首先需要了解德国新冠疫苗加强针的背景情况。加强针的推出是为了提高保护力，尤其是针对易感人群，如老年人和养老院居民，因为随着时间推移，初始疫苗的免疫力可能会减弱。与所有疫苗和医疗干预措施一样，新冠疫苗也可能产生副作用，但根据卫生部门的数据，严重不良事件极为罕见。

该社交媒体帖子的核心内容是，据称由一名医生撰写的一封信，详细描述了某位居民在接种第三剂新冠疫苗后死亡，另外两名居民需要进行心肺复苏。然而，该帖子并未说明事件发生的具体日期、涉及人员的身份以及医疗事件的具体情况。值得注意的是，该帖子将这些事件归因于加强针接种，但并未提供医学证据证明直接的因果关系。

核查此类说法需要仔细查阅官方声明、医疗记录（如可获得）以及卫生部门的背景信息。在以往类似报告中，有关接种疫苗后发生死亡或严重事件的报告通常由当地卫生部门调查，而在德国，此类调查由保罗·埃利希研究所负责，该机构负责监测疫苗安全性。在绝大多数案例中，调查结果显示，与接种疫苗同时发生的不良事件通常与老年人的基础健康状况或整体脆弱性有关，而非疫苗本身所致。

鉴于养老院居民普遍年龄较大，且健康状况复杂，死亡或医疗紧急事件的发生并不罕见。因此，仅因时间上的关联并不能自动推断因果关系。卫生部门强调，必须进行全面的医学评估，以判断疫苗是否在这些事件中发挥了作用。在正式调查结果或尸检报告公布之前，无法确认该加强针剂量是否导致了该帖子中提及的死亡或心肺复苏事件。

此外，公共卫生数据显示，对于老年人群而言，新冠疫苗包括加强针的益处仍超过其风险，因为老年人群本身面临更高的病毒严重感染风险。

总之，尽管该帖子提到了一封关于奥伯豪森某养老院接种加强针后出现不良事件的医生信件，但目前尚无公开证据证明第三剂疫苗直接导致了死亡和两次心肺复苏。在卫生部门通过深入调查确认之前，此类报告应谨慎对待。新冠疫苗的安全记录依然良好，尤其是在高风险人群中。

A recent social media post asserts that the data on the number of deaths in 2020 and the use of intensive care beds does not indicate the existence of a pandemic. Additionally, it questions the validity of infection figures derived from PCR tests, suggesting that these numbers are unusable. This article examines these claims in depth, providing context and an analysis of the available evidence.

To begin, the claim centers on two main points: first, that mortality and intensive care unit (ICU) usage data from 2020 do not support the existence of a pandemic; and second, that PCR test results for COVID-19 infections are unreliable and thus unusable for tracking the pandemic.

On the issue of mortality and ICU usage, it is important to understand the context of global health in 2020. The World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic in March 2020 amid rising infections, hospitalizations, and deaths worldwide. Many countries reported a significant increase in overall mortality compared to previous years, a phenomenon known as excess mortality. This measure includes not only deaths directly attributed to COVID-19, but also those resulting from healthcare system strain and delayed treatment for other conditions.

Data collected by national and international health authorities throughout 2020 indicate that many regions experienced substantial excess deaths, far above the averages observed in previous years. In some countries, these spikes corresponded closely with COVID-19 outbreaks. Hospitals in particularly hard-hit areas reported overwhelming numbers of patients requiring intensive care, leading to shortages of ICU beds and medical staff. While the distribution of these impacts was uneven—some regions saw less pronounced spikes, or managed to control outbreaks more effectively—the overall global trend showed clear signals of a public health emergency.

Regarding the claim about PCR tests, these tests became the gold standard for detecting active COVID-19 infections due to their sensitivity in identifying genetic material from the virus. While it is true that PCR tests can detect small amounts of viral RNA, and that the interpretation of “positive” results depends on factors such as cycle threshold values and timing of the test, these tests are widely recognized by medical experts as reliable for diagnosing current infections when used appropriately. Concerns about false positives or detecting non-infectious viral fragments have been addressed by refining testing protocols and interpretation guidelines. The reported infection figures, while not without limitations, have provided valuable data for tracking the spread of the virus and informing public health responses.

In summary, the assertion that death and ICU data from 2020 do not indicate a pandemic, and that PCR test data are unusable, is not supported by the broader context and available evidence. Excess mortality and ICU usage data from multiple countries demonstrate the significant impact of COVID-19, while PCR testing, despite some limitations, has been an essential tool in measuring and managing the pandemic. The scientific consensus remains that the data from 2020 clearly reflect the occurrence and scope of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Nesen izvadīts sociālos tīklos paziņojums apgalvo, ka 2020. gadā iegūtās datus par nāves gadījumiem un intensīvās aprūpes gultu izmantošanu neatklāj pandēmijas pastāvēšanu. Turklāt paziņojums jautā par izmaiņu patiesību infekcijas datu, kas iegūti ar PCR testiem, un uzskata, ka šie skaitļi nav izmantojami. Šis raksts pārskata šos apgalvojumus, sniedz kontekstu un analīzi pieejamajam pierādījumam.

Sākumā apgalvojums centra ir divi galvenie punkti: pirmais, ka 2020. gada nāves un intensīvās aprūpes vietas izmantošanas dati neapstiprina pandēmijas pastāvēšanu; otrais, ka PCR testu rezultāti par koronavīrusa infekcijām nav ticami un tādēļ nav izmantojami pandēmijas uzraudzībai.

Attiecībā uz nāves un intensīvās aprūpes izmantošanas datiem svarīgi saprast globālās veselības stāvokli 2020. gadā. Pasaules Veselības organizācija (PVO) 2020. gada martsā deklarēja, ka koronavīrusa infekcija ir pandēmija, atbriedzot infekciju, slimības izplatīšanās un nāves pieaugums visā pasaulē. Daudzi valsti izvēstīja nozīmīgu nāves pieaugumu salīdzinājumā ar iepriekšējiem gadiem, par ko runā pārmērīga nāve. Šis mērs ietver ne tikai nāves, kas tieši saistītas ar koronavīrusu, bet arī nāves, kas izraisītas veselības sistēmas pārmērīgai slodzei un atkavētajam citu slimību ārstēšanai.

2020. gada dati, kas iegūti valstu un starptautisku veselības iestāžu pārvaldībā, rāda, ka daudzas reģionālas izvēstīja pārmērīgu nāves skaitu, kura bija daudz augstāka nekā iepriekšējos gados. Dažās valstīs šie pieaugumi atbilda cieši koronavīrusa izplatīšanās vienādībām. Veselības iestādes, kas bija vairāk ietekmētas, ziņoja par pārmērīgu pacientu skaitu, kas prasīja intensīvās aprūpes, kas izraisīja intensīvās aprūpes gultu un medicīnas darbinieku trūkumu. Ietekmes sadalījums bija nesamērīgs – dažos reģionos šie pieaugumi bija mazāki, vai nu valdība efektīvāk kontrolēja izplatīšanos, bet vispārējā pasaulē bija skaidri izteikts sabiedrības veselības krīzes simptomi.

Attiecībā uz PCR testu apgalvojumu, šie testi kļuva par standartu aktīvu koronavīrusa infekcijas atklāšanai, jo tos izmanto, lai identificētu vīrusa DNS materiālu. Patiesībā ir tāda, ka PCR testi var atklāt pat mazas vīrusa RNA daudzumus, un pozitīvo rezultātu interpretācija atkarīga no faktoriem, piemēram, cikla slēguma vērtībām un testa veikšanas laikpunktam. Tomēr šie testi tiek uzskatīti par ticamiem infekcijas diagnostikai, kad tie tiek izmantoti pareizi. Jautājumi par nepareizi pozitīvus rezultātus un neinficējošu vīrusa fragmentu izpēti ir tika atbildēti, uzlabojot testu protokolus un interpretācijas noteikumus. Izvadītie infekcijas dati, apmierinājoties ar savām ierobežojumiem, sniedza vērtīgu informāciju par vīrusa izplatīšanās uzraudzību un sabiedrības veselības reakcijas izstrādi.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims that vaccinated individuals in intensive care units (ICUs) are counted as COVID-19 cases only if they exhibit clinical symptoms, whereas unvaccinated individuals are included in the statistics of the Robert Koch Institute (RKI) simply by testing positive for the virus. This assertion has sparked debate and confusion regarding how COVID-19 cases are recorded and reported in Germany, particularly by the RKI, which serves as the country’s national public health institute.

To evaluate this claim, it is essential to understand how COVID-19 data is collected and categorized by the RKI, and whether vaccination status influences the criteria for reporting cases, especially those requiring intensive care.

**Background and Data Collection**

The RKI is responsible for monitoring the spread of COVID-19 in Germany, collecting data from hospitals, laboratories, and local health authorities. The institute’s reporting system distinguishes between laboratory-confirmed cases, hospitalizations, and severe disease outcomes such as admissions to ICUs or deaths. The vaccination status of patients is recorded separately to assess the effectiveness of vaccines and monitor breakthrough infections.

Typically, a COVID-19 case is defined by a positive PCR test, regardless of symptoms. Hospitalizations and ICU admissions are reported as severe outcomes if COVID-19 is deemed the primary reason for admission. However, there can be cases where a patient is admitted for another medical reason and incidentally tests positive for COVID-19. In such situations, local health authorities may still report the case if the positive test is confirmed, but the clinical diagnosis, including symptoms and reason for ICU admission, is crucial for further categorization.

**Analyzing the Claim**

The social media post suggests a discrepancy in how vaccinated and unvaccinated patients are counted in ICU statistics. It implies that vaccinated patients must exhibit clinical symptoms to be counted as COVID-19 cases in ICU, while unvaccinated patients are counted solely based on a positive test result.

Current RKI guidelines do not differentiate reporting thresholds based on vaccination status. Both vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals are categorized as COVID-19 cases if they test positive. When it comes to severe outcomes like ICU admissions, the clinical relevance of COVID-19 is assessed for all patients, regardless of vaccine status. If a person is admitted to the ICU with a positive COVID-19 test but without symptoms or illness attributable to COVID-19, the case may be classified as an incidental infection rather than a COVID-19 ICU admission. This applies equally to vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals.

**Conclusion**

The claim that vaccinated people in ICUs are only counted as COVID-19 cases if symptomatic, while unvaccinated people are counted based solely on a positive test, is misleading. The RKI’s reporting standards do not distinguish between vaccinated and unvaccinated patients in this manner. Both groups are initially counted as COVID-19 cases based on laboratory confirmation. For ICU statistics, the determining factor is whether COVID-19 is the primary reason for admission, not the vaccination status or presence of symptoms alone. The distinction is based on clinical relevance, ensuring accurate data on severe cases, and is applied irrespective of whether a patient is vaccinated or not.

**Fondashon y Kolléi di Datos**

Sin embargo, ta kazes ku un paciente ta entran pa otro rason médiku y testáu positivu ku COVID-19 incidentalmente. En esas situashon, autoridades di saúd lokal ta reportáu el kazu si el test positivu ta konfirmáu, pero el diagnostiku klinikal, inclusive simptomas y rason pa entran di ICU, ta esensial pa kategorizashon posterior.

**Analizando e ta Afirmashon**

E post di social media sugeri ku di diferensia en manera ku individuos vacunáu y no vacunáu ta kontáu en estatístikas di ICU. Cuanto a resultados grave como entran di ICU, el relevansi klinikal di COVID-19 ta evaluáu pa todos los pacientes, sin importa el estatus di vacunashon. Si un persona ta entran di ICU ku test positivu di COVID-19 pero sin simptomas o enfermedad atribuibel a el virus, el kazu ta klasifikáu como infeksion incidental, no como entran di ICU pa el virus. Eso ta aplicáu igualmente pa individuos vacunáu y no vacunáu.

**Konklusión**

E afirmashon ku individuos vacunáu en ICUs ta kontáu como kazes di COVID-19 solo si ta esibí simptomas, mientras ke individuos no vacunáu ta kontáu basáu solamente en test positivu, ta engaño. El estándar di reportáu di RKI no diferensia entre individuos vacunáu y no vacunáu en es manera. Ambos grupos ta kontáu inicialmente como kazes di COVID-19 basáu en konfirmashon labóriu. Pa estatístikas di ICU, el factor determinante ta si el COVID-19 ta razon primaria pa entran, no el estatus di vacunashon o presensia di simptomas solamente. E diferensia ta basáu en relevansi klinikal, garantíando datos akurat di kazes grave, y ta aplicáu sin importa si un paciente ta vacunáu o no.
